column3: Close to the Hebrew.
Hebrew has the singular “my thought”; BSB has “my thoughts.”
Hebrew uses completed forms for searching the path and being acquainted with the ways; BSB uses present forms.
Hebrew says “for there is no word on my tongue; behold”; BSB supplies the temporal wording “even before.”
Hebrew says “palm”; BSB uses the broader “hand.” The hemming in is also a completed action.
Close to the Hebrew.
Hebrew says “from Your Spirit” and “from Your face”; BSB makes escape explicit and uses “presence.”
The second clause ends “behold, You”; BSB repeats “You are there.”
Hebrew says “lift the wings of dawn”; BSB has “rise on the wings of the dawn.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Hebrew says darkness will crush the speaker, and “night is light around me”; BSB has darkness hiding him and light becoming night.
Hebrew closes with the parallel “as the darkness, so the light”; BSB expands it to “for darkness is as light to You.”
Hebrew explicitly names the kidneys and acquiring them; BSB says “formed my inmost being.”
Hebrew says “my soul knows”; BSB has simply “I know.” It begins with giving thanks rather than praising.
Hebrew says “my bone” and “embroidered”; BSB has “my frame” and “woven together.”
The printed Hebrew ends “and for him one among them”; BSB has “before one of them came to be.” Hebrew does not expressly add “my” before “days.”
Hebrew has the plural “their sums”; BSB has the singular “their sum.”
Hebrew says “I have awakened”; BSB has “when I awake.” “Grains” is not explicitly stated before “sand.”
Hebrew has a singular “wicked man” and the image “men of blood”; BSB renders the latter “bloodthirsty men.”
“Your name” in BSB’s second clause is not expressed in the printed Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
Hebrew says they “became enemies to me”; BSB says “I count them as my enemies.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Hebrew calls it a “way of pain”; BSB uses “offensive way.”
